properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored BIP-0038 implementation (libs/bitcoinjs-bip38) used by the wallet for passphrase-encrypted Bitcoin private keys. All 4 sites live: encryptRaw line 68 and decrypt paths 117/187/195 use aes-256-ecb with the second scrypt-derived half as key, encrypting the XOR-masked 32-byte private key. ECB with no IV is what BIP-0038 mandates (single fixed-size block, half-key-derived independently), so the classic ECB pattern-leak does not apply; changeable only by deviating from the spec. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CryptoJS-style OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey single-round MD5 KDF shipped inside the libs/combined bundle (via crypto-js / evp_bytestokey dependencies). It is what a naive CryptoJS.AES.encrypt(passphrase) would use to derive its key+IV. No direct passphrase-encrypt call site found in src/; presence recorded per the dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored Bootstrap/jQuery internals: Bootstrap's getUID() builds a unique tooltip DOM-element id, jQuery's expando seeds its DOM data-cache key, Sizzle's dirrunsUnique disambiguates its selector cache. Wallet entropy never comes from these — the app's own mnemonic generator explicitly requires crypto.getRandomValues (src/js/jsbip39.js:62-65) and src/js/index.js:692 uses it. Real Math.random uses, non-security purpose.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA capability ships via jsrsasign@8.0.24, declared in the libs/combined lockfile and vendored in the browser bundle. Available in the shipped library; no RSA call site found in the application code (this is an offline mnemonic/key-derivation page). jsrsasign 8.0.24 is a 2018-era release — the pinned version is the posture-relevant fact, since later jsrsasign releases fixed RSA/OAEP and signature-verification CVEs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed KDF: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 512-bit output. Iteration count is read at runtime from the .pbkdf2-rounds <select> in src/index.html:133 (BIP39 standard value 2048). 2048 rounds is far below OWASP password-hashing minimums but is exactly what BIP-0039 specifies for high-entropy (128-bit) mnemonic input, so it is protocol-standard, not a weakness introduced here.
